info.name: abd-ecomm-nestjs
info.description:
Our API layer on top of Shopify.

HOW TO USE — CUSTOMER SIDE:
1. Run `Auth / 1. Request OTP` — devCode is saved automatically
2. Run `Auth / 2. Verify OTP` — the code is filled in for you, and accessToken + refreshToken are saved
3. Every other customer request now works — the Bearer token is attached automatically

HOW TO USE — ADMIN SIDE:
1. Set the `adminEmail` and `adminPassword` collection variables
2. Run `Admin — Auth / 1. Login` — adminToken is saved automatically
3. Every `Admin — *` folder now works

⚠️ THE TWO TOKENS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE, and that is the point.
Customer auth and admin auth use different signing secrets and differently
named Passport strategies. A customer token gets 401 on every /admin route,
and an admin token gets 401 on every customer route. Mixing them fails loudly
instead of quietly passing. The app even refuses to boot if JWT_ADMIN_SECRET
and JWT_ACCESS_SECRET are the same value.

All tokens are stored in collection variables, so there is nothing to copy by hand.

A NOTE ON THE DOCUMENTATION IN THIS COLLECTION:
Every request documents where each response key comes from, using this notation:

    responseKey  ← sourceField

The source is either a Shopify GraphQL field, a Postgres column, or a value
we compute ourselves. Comments cannot live inside the request body itself —
Postman sends the raw body to the server as-is, so a `//` comment would
break JSON parsing. All documentation therefore lives in each request's
description, visible in the panel on the right.

request.description:
Status of Postgres, Redis and the Shopify configuration.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

status             ← "ok" when postgres AND redis are both "up",
                     otherwise "degraded"

services.postgres  ← whether Prisma's `SELECT 1` succeeded
services.redis     ← the reply to a Redis PING

services.shopify   ← A CONFIG CHECK ONLY — "configured" | "not-configured"
                     ⚠️ Shopify is deliberately NOT pinged here. The health
                     check runs every few seconds, and pinging Shopify would
                     drain its cost bucket. So "configured" means "the
                     credentials are present", NOT "Shopify is reachable".

timestamp          ← the server's current time, ISO 8601

────────────────────────────────
NOTES
────────────────────────────────
This endpoint is exempt from rate limiting (@SkipThrottle) — the platform
health check hits it constantly and must never be throttled.

This is the path configured as Render's Health Check Path:
  /api/v1/health

request.description:
Sends a one-time password to a phone number or an email address.

────────────────────────────────
BODY
────────────────────────────────

identifier   A phone number OR an email address — both go in this SINGLE
             field. The app does not need two separate screens; the server
             works out which one it is and normalises it.
             All of these are accepted:
               "9876543210", "+91 98765 43210", "user@gmail.com"
             A phone number without a country code gets
             DEFAULT_COUNTRY_CODE (default IN) applied.
             Required, max 255 characters.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

sent                ← ALWAYS `true`.
                      The response is identical whether or not the user
                      exists. Otherwise someone could submit phone numbers
                      one by one and learn which are registered — an
                      account enumeration attack.

sentTo              ← the destination, masked: "+91******3210"
                      Lets the app say "we sent a code to this number"
                      without echoing the full value back.

expiresAt           ← now + OTP_TTL_SECONDS (default 300s), as ISO 8601
resendAfterSeconds  ← OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS (default 60)
                      The app should disable its "Resend" button for this
                      many seconds.

devCode             ← ONLY present when OTP_EXPOSE_IN_RESPONSE=true.
                      ⚠️ This key DOES NOT EXIST in production, so the app
                      must never depend on it. The test script saves it to
                      `{{devCode}}` automatically.
                      When OTP_EXPOSE_IN_RESPONSE=false, the code is printed
                      to the server logs instead (the console OTP sender).

────────────────────────────────
RATE LIMITS — THREE SEPARATE LAYERS
────────────────────────────────
1. Route level:    10 requests/min per IP (@Throttle)
2. Per identifier: OTP_MAX_PER_IDENTIFIER_PER_HOUR (default 5)
3. Per IP:         OTP_MAX_PER_IP_PER_HOUR (default 20)

Breaching any of them returns 429. The counters live in Redis.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
400 — identifier missing, or longer than 255 characters
429 — any of the three rate limits above was exceeded

request.description:
Verifies the OTP and logs the user in.

📌 THERE IS NO SEPARATE SIGNUP ENDPOINT. If the user is new they are created
here; if they already exist as an IMPORTED Shopify record, that record is
activated instead — keeping all of their history.

────────────────────────────────
BODY
────────────────────────────────

identifier   Must be THE SAME value sent to `1. Request OTP`. The OTP is
             bound to that identifier, so anything else will not match.
             Required, max 255 characters.

code         The one-time password. Filled in from `{{devCode}}` during
             development. Length is OTP_LENGTH (default 6); the field
             accepts 4-8 characters.

deviceId     Ties the session to a device, which is what makes per-device
             logout and session auditing possible. Optional, but the app
             should always send a stable value. Max 128 characters.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

isNewUser             ← whether this is the first ever login for this
                        identifier. When `true` the app should show the
                        app. There is no registration form — send them to the home screen.

linkedShopifyRecords  ← how many EXISTING Shopify customer records were
                        attached to this account during login. Greater than
                        zero for someone who previously checked out on the
                        website as a guest.

customer              ← the profile object — exactly the same shape as
                        `3. Me`, documented there.

tokens.accessToken    ← a JWT, valid for JWT_ACCESS_TTL (default 900s).
                        Send it on protected requests as:
                          Authorization: Bearer <token>

tokens.refreshToken   ← an opaque random string (NOT a JWT), valid for
                        REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_DAYS (default 60 days).

tokens.expiresIn      ← remaining lifetime of accessToken, IN SECONDS
tokens.tokenType      ← always "Bearer"

The test script stores accessToken and refreshToken in collection variables,
so nothing needs to be copied manually.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
400 — code is not 4-8 characters
401 — wrong code, expired code, or OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 5) exhausted
429 — 20 requests/min per IP exceeded

The signed-in user's profile, including every verified email and phone.

Requires the Authorization header.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

id                   ← OUR Customer.id (a UUID).
                       This is never a Shopify id. Shopify's numeric ids do
                       not leave the server.

phone                ← Customer.primaryPhone (the verified one)
                       `null` if the user signed up with an email.

emailVerified        ← whether any verified identity of type EMAIL exists.
                       ⚠️ There is NO `email` key in this response, by
                       design. An email only ever reaches an account by
                       being OTP-verified, so the address itself lives
                       in `verifiedIdentifiers` — the entry with type
                       "EMAIL". An unverified email cannot exist on
                       this system at all.
phoneVerified        ← whether any verified identity of type PHONE exists

firstName            ← Customer.firstName. Filled in automatically from
                       the first delivery address the user saves, or by
                       `4. Update profile`, or from a linked Shopify
                       record. Null until one of those happens.
lastName             ← Customer.lastName, same three sources

hasPassword          ← whether Customer.passwordHash is set.
                       Always `false` in Phase 1 — login is OTP only. The
                       field exists so the app does not break when password
                       login is added later.

verifiedIdentifiers  ← [{ type: "PHONE" | "EMAIL", value }]
                       Every verified identifier on this account.
                       📌 Past orders are matched ONLY against these values.
                       An unverified email is never used for matching.

createdAt            ← Customer.createdAt, as ISO 8601

────────────────────────────────
WHAT THE APP SHOULD DO
────────────────────────────────
When `emailVerified` is `false`, show "Verify your email to see older
orders" and start the flow in the `Identity linking` folder.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
401 — missing, malformed or expired accessToken

Profile edit (screen 36).

⚠️ THIS IS NOT A SIGNUP STEP. There is no registration screen any more —
after `2. Verify OTP` the user goes straight into the app, whether or not
`isNewUser` is true. Their name is filled in automatically from the first
delivery address they save, so most users never open this screen at all.

────────────────────────────────
BODY — every field is OPTIONAL (partial update)
────────────────────────────────

firstName    Max 80 characters. Omit it and the stored value is unchanged.
lastName     Max 80 characters. Omit it and the stored value is unchanged.

             Sending either one also pushes the name to the customer's
             Shopify record, so the store admin and order confirmation
             emails show what the user actually typed. Best-effort: if
             Shopify is down the profile still saves and the next update
             re-syncs it.

gender       Screen 36, "Additional Information". A free string, max 32
             characters — the app decides which options to offer.

⚠️ THERE IS NO `email` FIELD ON THIS ENDPOINT. It was removed, and so was
the column behind it.

Storing an address the user merely typed was the whole problem: anyone can
type a stranger's address, and once it sits on the account something will
eventually treat it as real. Hiding it was not enough — it is gone.

An email reaches an account through exactly one path:

    POST /auth/identities/request-otp  →  POST /auth/identities/verify

That is also the step that finds the user's past orders. Send them there.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

The updated profile, in exactly the same shape as `3. Me`:

id                   ← our Customer.id (UUID)
phone                ← Customer.primaryPhone
emailVerified        ← UNCHANGED by this call. Nothing on this endpoint
                       can alter it — only identity linking can.
phoneVerified        ← whether a verified PHONE identity exists
firstName            ← what you just sent, or the previous value
lastName             ← what you just sent, or the previous value
gender               ← what you just sent, or the previous value
hasPassword          ← always false in Phase 1
verifiedIdentifiers  ← unchanged by this call
createdAt            ← Customer.createdAt

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
400 — invalid email, a field over its length limit, or an unknown field
      (unknown properties are rejected, not silently dropped)
401 — missing or expired accessToken

request.description:
Exchanges a refresh token for a fresh pair of tokens.

────────────────────────────────
BODY
────────────────────────────────

refreshToken   The MOST RECENT refresh token. The test scripts keep
               `{{refreshToken}}` up to date for you.
               Required, max 512 characters.

deviceId       Optional, but send THE SAME value used at login so the
               session stays attached to the same device.
               Max 128 characters.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

accessToken    ← a NEW JWT (JWT_ACCESS_TTL, default 900s)
refreshToken   ← a NEW refresh token. The one you just sent is revoked
                 at that very moment.
expiresIn      ← remaining lifetime of accessToken, in seconds
tokenType      ← always "Bearer"

────────────────────────────────
📌 ROTATION — WORTH UNDERSTANDING
────────────────────────────────
Every refresh destroys the old token and issues a new one.

If a token that has ALREADY BEEN USED shows up again, there is only one
reasonable explanation: it was stolen. When that happens the entire token
family for that user is revoked and they must log in again.

So the app must always persist the LATEST refresh token. An old copy left
lying around in storage will log the user out if it is ever replayed.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
401 — unknown, expired, or already-used refresh token
      (an already-used one also revokes the whole family)

Ends the session on this device only.

────────────────────────────────
BODY
────────────────────────────────

refreshToken   OPTIONAL, max 512 characters.
               When supplied, that specific token is revoked, which ends
               this device's session.
               When omitted nothing is revoked server-side — you still get
               a 200, but the session remains alive.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

success   ← always `true`, whether or not a token was supplied

────────────────────────────────
⚠️ THE APP MUST ALSO DO THIS
────────────────────────────────
The accessToken is a JWT, which means it is STATELESS. After logout it stays
valid until it expires on its own (JWT_ACCESS_TTL, default 15 minutes) —
the server cannot recall it.

So on logout the app MUST delete both tokens from local storage. Calling
this endpoint alone is not enough.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
401 — missing or expired accessToken

Ends every session on every device. No body — the user is identified from
the accessToken.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

sessionsRevoked   ← how many refresh tokens were revoked, which is the
                    number of devices that were signed in.
                    The app can show "Signed out of 3 devices".
                    `0` simply means there were no other live sessions.

────────────────────────────────
WHEN TO USE IT
────────────────────────────────
The "Log out of all devices" button, and after any security-sensitive
change such as a phone number update.

⚠️ Like `6. Logout`, this only revokes REFRESH tokens. Access tokens on
other devices keep working until they expire on their own — at most
JWT_ACCESS_TTL (default 15 minutes).

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
401 — missing or expired accessToken

item.name: Identity linking
item.description:
The "I can't see my old orders" flow.

The user signed in with their phone, but their older website orders were
placed as a guest under a DIFFERENT email address. Verifying that email here
attaches those orders to their account.

Security: linking only ever happens against a VERIFIED identifier —
otherwise anyone could claim someone else's order history.

════════════════════════════════
WHEN TO CALL THIS IN THE APP
════════════════════════════════
This is not a settings-screen afterthought. WHEN you ask decides how much
mess the backend has to clean up afterwards.

The store's numbers say why it matters. Of the 106 customers who have
actually ordered: 62 have only an email, 43 have only a phone, and exactly
1 has both. Neither channel alone finds everyone — so a phone-only app user
is very often someone who already exists in Shopify under an email.

When that person signs up by phone we create a NEW Shopify record for them.
Verifying their email is what reunites the two:

  Email verified BEFORE their first order
      -> the record we created is still empty
      -> it is DELETED. Clean, cheap, nothing left behind.

  Email verified AFTER an order
      -> that record now has an order on it and cannot be deleted
      -> the two records must be MERGED inside Shopify instead
      -> merges can be BLOCKED (subscriptions, gift cards, store credit),
         and a blocked merge leaves a permanent duplicate customer

So, in priority order:

  1. Before checkout, if only a phone is verified  <- THE main moment, and
     the last clean one. Ask here even if you ask nowhere else.
  2. A banner on the Orders screen whenever emailVerified is false
  3. On "import my old addresses", which needs a verified email anyway
  4. Profile > manage email/phone  <- keep it, but do not rely on it

There is no onboarding prompt in this list on purpose. Signup collects
nothing but a phone number, so the first natural moment to ask is checkout.

⚠️ DO NOT BLOCK Orders or Addresses behind this flow. A phone-only customer
can place an order in the app and see it in GET /orders — checkout sends
their verified phone as the buyer identity. Gate those screens and you are
hiding a customer's own orders from them. Email is needed for PRE-APP data
only, so prompt, never gate.

NEVER call it silently in the background — it sends a real OTP, so it must
always be user-initiated. Let the user tap "Verify".

════════════════════════════════
HOW THE APP KNOWS WHETHER TO ASK
════════════════════════════════
Straight from 'Auth / 3. Me'. No extra field is needed:

  emailVerified = false  ->  "Add your email to see your past orders"
  emailVerified = true   ->  nothing to show, done

The profile has no `email` key, so the input always opens empty. Nothing is
lost: the app never collected an address to prefill it with. A verified
email, once linked, shows up in `verifiedIdentifiers` as the entry with
type "EMAIL".

request.description:
Sends an OTP to an ADDITIONAL email or phone that an already signed-in user
wants to prove they own. Requires the Authorization header.

────────────────────────────────
BODY
────────────────────────────────

identifier   The email or phone number to verify, held in
             `{{linkIdentifier}}`.
             ⚠️ This is normally DIFFERENT from the identifier they logged
             in with — typically the email used for guest checkout on the
             website.
             Required, max 255 characters.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

sent                ← always `true`, for the same enumeration-safety reason
                      as `Auth / 1. Request OTP`
sentTo              ← the destination, masked: "o***@example.com"
expiresAt           ← now + OTP_TTL_SECONDS (default 300s), ISO 8601
resendAfterSeconds  ← OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS (default 60)
devCode             ← only when OTP_EXPOSE_IN_RESPONSE=true; the test script
                      saves it to `{{linkDevCode}}`

────────────────────────────────
RATE LIMITS
────────────────────────────────
10 requests/min per IP at the route level, plus the same per-identifier and
per-IP OTP limits described in `Auth / 1. Request OTP`.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
401 — missing or expired accessToken
429 — any OTP rate limit exceeded

Once verification succeeds — and not before — the old Shopify records
belonging to that identifier are attached to the user's account.

────────────────────────────────
BODY
────────────────────────────────

identifier   Must be THE SAME value sent to
             `1. Request OTP for another email/phone`.
             Required, max 255 characters.

code         The one-time password, filled in from `{{linkDevCode}}`.
             4-8 characters.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

linkedShopifyRecords  ← how many EXISTING Shopify customer records this
                        verification attached. `0` is a perfectly normal
                        result — it just means Shopify has no record under
                        that email.

importedAddresses     ← how many addresses were pulled in from the newly
                        linked Shopify records (address book + past orders).
                        Also normally `0` for a brand-new customer.

customer              ← the updated profile, same shape as `Auth / 3. Me`.
                        The newly verified identifier now appears in
                        `verifiedIdentifiers`, and for an email
                        `emailVerified` flips to `true`.

Show these two numbers to the user — "found 5 past orders and 2 addresses" —
otherwise nothing visibly happened and the step feels pointless. Then
refresh the Orders and Addresses screens.

────────────────────────────────
WHAT HAPPENS IN SHOPIFY (email only)
────────────────────────────────
Verifying an EMAIL also triggers a reconcile. If Shopify already has an
older customer under that email, it becomes the primary record and the
phone-only record we created at signup has to go. How it goes depends on
one thing — whether an order was placed on it:

  no orders yet  ->  deleted
  has orders     ->  merged into the older record, phone carried across

A merge is asynchronous and can be refused by Shopify (subscriptions, gift
cards, store credit). If it is refused, the duplicate stays and is logged
for manual review.

⚠️ None of this can fail the request. The email is verified either way, and
the app's order history is correct either way — both records stay linked
on our side. A failed reconcile only ever leaves a duplicate in the Shopify
admin, never a gap for the user.

────────────────────────────────
🔒 WHY THERE IS AN EXTRA OWNERSHIP CHECK
────────────────────────────────
The server verifies that the OTP was issued to the SAME user who is now
presenting it. Without that check an attacker could request an OTP for
their own address, then submit it using ANOTHER user's accessToken — and
quietly attach their email to that person's account.

This is also why linking only works against verified identifiers — and why
nothing else on the API accepts an email at all. There is no unverified
address anywhere for order matching to accidentally trust.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
400 — code is not 4-8 characters
401 — wrong or expired code, OR the OTP was issued to a different user
409 — this email/phone is already verified on ANOTHER account.
      The user cannot resolve this themselves — send them to support.
      Do not retry.
429 — 20 requests/min per IP exceeded

item.name: Addresses
item.description:
Every endpoint here requires authentication.

Addresses live in OUR Postgres database, not in Shopify — so they come with
us during the migration and we never have to reach back to Shopify for
them.

request.description:
All of the user's saved addresses. The default one always comes first.

The response is a plain ARRAY — there is no pagination, because nobody has
hundreds of addresses.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key of an item comes from
────────────────────────────────

id            ← our Address.id (UUID). Never a Shopify id.
                This is the value used as `{{addressId}}` in update and
                delete below.

firstName     ← Address.firstName   (may be null)
lastName      ← Address.lastName    (may be null)
phone         ← Address.phone       (may be null)

line1         ← Address.line1       (always present)
line2         ← Address.line2       (may be null)
city          ← Address.city        (always present)
province      ← Address.province    (may be null)
zip           ← Address.zip         (always present)
country       ← Address.country     (always present)
countryCode   ← Address.countryCode (ISO 2-letter, may be null)

isDefault     ← Address.isDefault
                Exactly one address has this set to `true`.

imported      ← computed as Address.importedFromOrder !== null
                `true`  = pulled automatically from a past order
                          (see `5. Import from past orders`)
                `false` = the user added it themselves
                The app can use this to show a "from your past order" badge.

📌 `provinceCode` exists in the database but is deliberately NOT returned —
the app has no use for it. Add it to the address mapper if that changes.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
401 — missing or expired accessToken

exec: // Save the id so update / set-default / delete can target it.

request.description:
Saves a new address for the signed-in user.

────────────────────────────────
BODY — which fields are required
────────────────────────────────

REQUIRED:
  line1          3-200 characters
  city           2-100 characters
  zip            3-20 characters
  country        2-100 characters (full name, e.g. "India")

OPTIONAL:
  firstName      max 80
  lastName       max 80
  phone          max 30
  line2          max 200
  province       max 100 (e.g. "Gujarat")
  provinceCode   max 10  (e.g. "GJ") — stored, but not returned
  countryCode    EXACTLY 2 characters, ISO (e.g. "IN")
  isDefault      boolean — see the rule below

⚠️ Unknown fields are REJECTED, not ignored. Sending anything outside this
list returns 400 with "property X should not exist".

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

The address that was created, in the same shape as `1. List`:

id            ← the newly generated Address.id (UUID); the test script
                saves it to `{{addressId}}`
firstName     ← what you sent, or null
lastName      ← what you sent, or null
phone         ← what you sent, or null
line1         ← what you sent
line2         ← what you sent, or null
city          ← what you sent
province      ← what you sent, or null
zip           ← what you sent
country       ← what you sent
countryCode   ← what you sent, or null
isDefault     ← `true` if this is the first address, or if you asked for it
imported      ← always `false` here — you added it by hand

────────────────────────────────
TWO BEHAVIOURS WORTH KNOWING
────────────────────────────────

1. THE FIRST address automatically becomes the default, even if you did not
   send `isDefault`.

2. DEDUPLICATION — sending the same address again does NOT create a
   duplicate; the existing row is updated instead. The fingerprint is built
   from line1 + line2 + city + zip + country, with case, spacing and
   punctuation stripped:

     "A-101, Shanti Nagar"   and   "a 101 shanti nagar"   →   THE SAME

   Why it matters: one address typically appears across many past orders.
   Without deduplication the import feature would show the user the same
   address fifteen times, turning a convenience into a nuisance.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
400 — a required field is missing, a length rule was broken, or an unknown
      field was included
401 — missing or expired accessToken

Partial update — any field you DO NOT send keeps its current value.

────────────────────────────────
URL
────────────────────────────────
:id   `{{addressId}}`, saved automatically by `2. Create`.
      Must be a valid UUID or the request fails with 400 before it ever
      reaches the database.

────────────────────────────────
BODY — every field is optional
────────────────────────────────

Same fields and the same limits as `2. Create`, except that line1, city,
zip and country are optional here too:

  firstName      max 80
  lastName       max 80
  phone          max 30
  line1          3-200
  line2          max 200
  city           2-100
  province       max 100
  provinceCode   max 10
  zip            3-20
  country        2-100
  countryCode    exactly 2
  isDefault      boolean — sending `true` promotes this address and demotes
                 the previous default, exactly like `4. Set default`

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

The updated address, same shape as `1. List`:

id            ← unchanged Address.id
firstName     ← new value if sent, otherwise the stored one
lastName      ← new value if sent, otherwise the stored one
phone         ← new value if sent, otherwise the stored one
line1         ← new value if sent, otherwise the stored one
line2         ← new value if sent, otherwise the stored one
city          ← new value if sent, otherwise the stored one
province      ← new value if sent, otherwise the stored one
zip           ← new value if sent, otherwise the stored one
country       ← new value if sent, otherwise the stored one
countryCode   ← new value if sent, otherwise the stored one
isDefault     ← Address.isDefault after the update
imported      ← Address.importedFromOrder !== null (editing an imported
                address does not clear this flag)

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
400 — :id is not a UUID, or a field broke a length rule
401 — missing or expired accessToken
404 — no such address, OR it belongs to a different user.
      🔒 Both cases return the same 404 on purpose. Distinguishing them
      would let someone probe ids to discover which addresses exist.

Promotes one address to be the default. No body is sent.

────────────────────────────────
URL
────────────────────────────────
:id   `{{addressId}}` — must be a valid UUID.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

success   ← always `true` when the address was found and updated

📌 The updated address is NOT returned. The app should either re-fetch
`1. List` or flip the flag in its local state itself.

────────────────────────────────
BEHAVIOUR
────────────────────────────────
Only one address is ever the default — the previous one is demoted in the
same operation, so there is never a moment with two defaults.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
400 — :id is not a UUID
401 — missing or expired accessToken
404 — no such address, or it belongs to a different user

item.description:
Becoming an influencer, and checking where the application stands.

IMPORTANT: an influencer is NOT a separate account. It is the same customer
with one extra capability, so every request here uses the ordinary customer
`{{accessToken}}` — there is no second login and no separate token.

Submits an application. Requires the customer to be logged in.

────────────────────────────────
BODY
────────────────────────────────

socialHandle     2-60 chars. A leading "@" and a full profile URL are both
                 stripped server-side, so "@priya.styles",
                 "priya.styles" and "https://instagram.com/priya.styles"
                 all store the same value. Letters, numbers, dots,
                 underscores and hyphens only.

socialPlatform   instagram | youtube | facebook
                 A plain string in the database, not an enum — a new
                 platform should not require a migration.

followerCount    0 to 500,000,000.
                 ⚠️ SELF-REPORTED, never verified. It only exists so the
                 admin can sort the queue; the admin still has to open
                 the profile and look.

panNumber        Indian PAN, format ABCDE1234F. Required because payouts
                 attract TDS. Uppercased and de-spaced server-side.
                 ⚠️ Never returned in full by any endpoint.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

id                ← the new InfluencerApplication.id (UUID)
                    Saved to {{applicationId}} by the test script.

status            ← always "PENDING" on a fresh application
socialHandle      ← normalised value that was stored
socialPlatform    ← what you sent
followerCount     ← what you sent
rejectionReason   ← null here; only populated after a rejection
submittedAt       ← createdAt, ISO 8601
reviewedAt        ← null until an admin acts
canReapplyAt      ← null unless this application was rejected

📌 The PAN you sent is NOT echoed back. Nothing returns it in full.

────────────────────────────────
RATE LIMIT
────────────────────────────────
5 requests/min. Deliberately tight: each one creates a row in a queue
that a human has to clear.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
400 — bad handle, bad PAN format, or follower count out of range
400 — rejected less than 30 days ago; the message says how long is left
401 — no customer token
409 — an application is already under review, or you are already a creator

The 409 for a duplicate is enforced twice: once by a readable check in
the service, and once by a partial unique index in Postgres that only
applies to PENDING rows. The index is what survives two taps arriving
at the same moment.

The most recent application for the signed-in customer.

RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

📌 Returns `null` — not 404 — when the customer has never applied.

                    `null` in every other case. The app should show the
                    date and disable the button until then.

WHAT THE APP SHOULD DO
────────────────────────────────
null       → show "Become a creator"
PENDING    → show "Under review", no action
REJECTED   → show rejectionReason and the canReapplyAt date
APPROVED   → open the Creator tab; use GET /influencer/me from then on

A suspended creator keeps their record and their wallet balance —

item.name: Admin — Auth
item.description:
ONE admin user. No roles, no admin_users table, no signup, no
"forgot password" — the credentials live in env.

⚠️ COMPLETELY SEPARATE from customer auth: different login, different signing
secret (JWT_ADMIN_SECRET), different token variable ({{adminToken}}).
A customer token gets 401 here. That is checked on boot too — if
JWT_ADMIN_SECRET equals JWT_ACCESS_SECRET the app refuses to start, because
otherwise a customer token would sail through with only the payload's `typ`
field standing in the way.

Set {{adminEmail}} and {{adminPassword}} first, then run "1. Login".

request.description:
Email + password, and an 8-hour token comes back.

────────────────────────────────
BODY
────────────────────────────────

email      must match ADMIN_EMAIL (case-insensitive)
password   verified against ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH (argon2id).
           Generate the hash with:  npm run admin:hash -- "your-password"

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE
────────────────────────────────

accessToken   ← JWT signed with JWT_ADMIN_SECRET, typ: "admin"
expiresIn     ← JWT_ADMIN_TTL (default 28800 = 8 hours)
tokenType     ← "Bearer"
admin.email   ← ADMIN_EMAIL

There is NO refresh token, on purpose. One person, sitting in a browser,
an 8-hour session — the whole rotation machinery buys nothing here.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
401 — "Email or password is incorrect". The SAME message for a wrong email
      and a wrong password, and both checks always run, so the response
      time does not reveal which half was right.
429 — 10 failed attempts from one IP locks it for 15 minutes. This is a
      separate layer from the throttler: that limits request rate, this
      limits password guessing.
503 — ADMIN_EMAIL is empty, so the admin panel is switched off entirely.

WHAT MOVES

Verified identities, Shopify links, addresses, wishlist, recently viewed,

The day-to-day support desk. "I never got my OTP" is the most
common call there is, and this folder answers it.

⚠️ The OTP code — and even its hash — is NEVER returned by any of these
endpoints. Give an admin a way to read codes and one day that way is how
someone gets into an account.

QUERY PARAMETERS

item.name: Admin — Notifications
item.description:
Push campaigns.

Order of work: "1. Estimate audience" → "3. Create campaign" → "6. SEND NOW".

⚠️ In development PUSH_PROVIDER=console, so campaigns report themselves as
sent while nothing actually leaves the machine — the messages are printed to
the server log. Before real users, PUSH_PROVIDER=fcm and an FcmPushSender are
required, otherwise the panel will happily show "sent" forever and nobody
will receive anything.

Device tokens come from the app — see the "Push notifications" folder.

request.description:
RUN THIS BEFORE SENDING ANYTHING.

Seeing "40,000 devices" should give an admin pause, and so should seeing
"4 devices" — both mean something is worth checking.

────────────────────────────────
BODY
────────────────────────────────
audience   ALL | SEGMENT | CUSTOMER
segment    required when audience = SEGMENT
customerId required when audience = CUSTOMER

────────────────────────────────
SEGMENTS
────────────────────────────────
ALL_USERS        everyone with a push token
ABANDONED_CART   cart has items and has not been touched for 24 hours
HAS_WISHLIST     at least one wishlist item
INACTIVE_30D     no login in 30 days (or never)
NEW_LAST_7D      joined in the last week

⚠️ Every segment also requires customer.status = ACTIVE, and that condition
must never be removed. Sending marketing push to someone who was blocked, or
to a duplicate row that was merged away, is the simplest and most
embarrassing mistake this feature can make.
status: DRAFT | SCHEDULED | SENDING | SENT | FAILED | CANCELLED

{
  "title": "Diwali Sale is live",
  "body": "Up to 40% off on sarees. Tap to shop.",
  "deepLink": "collection:sarees",
  "audience": "SEGMENT",
  "segment": "HAS_WISHLIST"
}

request.description:
Creating does NOT send. "/send" is a separate call, on purpose.

────────────────────────────────
BODY
────────────────────────────────
title       max 100 chars. Android's tray shows roughly 40-50, so the panel
            should preview it — the API will not silently truncate.
body        max 500
deepLink    "product:blue-saree" | "collection:sarees" | "order:PBG1036" |
            "url:https://…"  — the app parses it.
            ⚠️ Not validated here. A wrong deep link means the app opens on
            home, which is bad; blocking the campaign over it is worse.
imageUrl    absolute URL
audience    ALL (default) | SEGMENT | CUSTOMER
scheduledAt ISO 8601 in the future → status becomes SCHEDULED.
            Leave it out → DRAFT.

totalTargets / sentCount / failedCount   ← the outcome
failures[]   ← ⚠️ ONLY FAILURES ARE STORED.

A 40,000-user broadcast would write 40,000 "sent" rows that nobody ever
reads, and one campaign would bloat the table. The success number lives in
sentCount. What is kept here is what someone actually needs: which token
broke and why. Tokens are stored masked (***last8).
Only DRAFT and SCHEDULED campaigns can be changed. Anything else returns 400 with its current status.

⚠️ THIS SENDS IMMEDIATELY AND CANNOT BE TAKEN BACK.

────────────────────────────────
WHAT HAPPENS
────────────────────────────────
1. The status is claimed atomically: DRAFT|SCHEDULED → SENDING. Two clicks,
   two tabs or two server instances race here, and the loser gets 400
   instead of the customer getting the notification twice.
2. Targets are resolved from the audience/segment (ACTIVE customers only).
3. Messages go out in batches of PUSH_BATCH_SIZE (default 100; FCM's own
   limit is 500).
4. Failures are recorded; tokens the provider calls permanently dead are
   DELETED, so future campaigns stop retrying corpses.
5. Counts are written and the status becomes SENT.

The audit entry is written BEFORE sending — if the server dies mid-send
there is still a record that this campaign was started.

⚠️ With PUSH_PROVIDER=console (the default) nothing leaves the machine: the
messages are printed to the server log and every one is reported as sent.
DRAFT or SCHEDULED only.

Sends every campaign whose scheduledAt has passed.

⚠️ THIS PROJECT HAS NO SCHEDULER. @nestjs/schedule was deliberately not added
— a whole package for one job, and a timer in every instance means the same
campaign goes out twice. An EXTERNAL CRON should hit this endpoint, say every
5 minutes (a Render cron job, or anything else).

Without that cron, scheduledAt campaigns sit in SCHEDULED forever.

Calling it twice at once is safe: the DRAFT|SCHEDULED → SENDING claim is a
single atomic updateMany.
A campaign that was already SENT cannot be deleted — it is history.
Reusable messages: "Order shipped", "Sale live".

⚠️ ADMIN AUTH IS COMPLETELY SEPARATE from customer auth. Different login,
different signing secret, different token variable ({{adminToken}}).
A customer token returns 401 here, and an admin token returns 401 on the
customer endpoints — the two strategies are named differently on purpose,
so mixing them fails loudly instead of quietly passing.

request.description:
There is exactly one admin, configured through environment variables —
no admin table, no signup, no roles, no "forgot password".

────────────────────────────────
BODY
────────────────────────────────
email      must match ADMIN_EMAIL
password   checked against ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH (argon2id), or
           ADMIN_PASSWORD in local development only

Create a hash with:  npm run admin:hash -- "your-password"

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────
accessToken   ← JWT signed with JWT_ADMIN_SECRET — a DIFFERENT secret
                from the customer one, so a customer token can never
                validate here even if a guard were wired wrongly
tokenType     ← always "Bearer"
expiresIn     ← JWT_ADMIN_TTL, default 28800 (8 hours)
admin.email   ← the configured ADMIN_EMAIL

📌 There is no refresh token. When the 8 hours are up, log in again.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
401 — "Email or password is incorrect" for BOTH wrong email and wrong
      password, and both are always checked in full so the response
      time cannot reveal which one was right
429 — too many attempts from this IP (ADMIN_MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS,
      locked for ADMIN_LOGIN_LOCK_SECONDS)
503 — ADMIN_EMAIL is empty, so the whole panel is switched off

RESPONSE

request.description:
The queue an admin works through. Offset pagination, not cursors —
the panel wants "Page 4 of 37", and this data is in our own Postgres.

────────────────────────────────
QUERY PARAMETERS
────────────────────────────────
status   PENDING | APPROVED | REJECTED. Omit to get everything.
         The panel should send PENDING by default so opening the screen
         shows only outstanding work.
sort     newest | oldest | followers (default newest)
search   matches handle, first name, last name, phone or email
page     from 1 (default 1)
limit    1-100 (default 25)

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE — where each key comes from
────────────────────────────────

items[].id               ← InfluencerApplication.id
items[].status           ← PENDING | APPROVED | REJECTED
items[].socialHandle     ← normalised handle, no leading @
items[].socialPlatform   ← instagram | youtube | facebook
items[].followerCount    ← ⚠️ self-reported, never verified
items[].profileUrl       ← BUILT from platform + handle, ready to open.
                           This is the point of the screen: the admin
                           clicks through and looks at the real account.
items[].panMasked        ← Application.panNumber as ABC****34F.
                           ⚠️ The full PAN is NEVER sent to the panel.
                           An admin screen sits open in an office where
                           anyone can read it. The full value is pulled
                           straight from the database at payout time.
items[].customerId       ← our Customer.id
items[].customerName     ← firstName + lastName, or null
items[].customerPhone    ← Customer.primaryPhone (verified)
items[].customerEmail    ← primaryEmail. Null when the creator has only
                           ever verified a phone number.
items[].rejectionReason  ← previous rejection text, if any
items[].submittedAt      ← createdAt
items[].reviewedAt       ← when a decision was made
items[].reviewedBy       ← the admin email that decided
items[].canReapplyAt     ← reviewedAt + 30 days, rejections only

page / limit / total / totalPages   ← standard admin pagination

One application in full. Same shape as a row from `3. Review queue` —
every key is documented there.

{{applicationId}} is filled in automatically by `3. Review queue`, or by
`Creator program / 1. Apply`.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
400 — :id is not a UUID
401 — missing or expired admin token
404 — no such application

Gate 1. After this call the customer's app opens its Creator tab.
No body — the acting admin comes from the token.

────────────────────────────────
WHAT HAPPENS
────────────────────────────────
In ONE transaction:
  1. the application becomes APPROVED, with reviewedBy and reviewedAt
  2. an Influencer row is created against that customer

Both together, deliberately. Split them and a failure in between leaves
an application marked APPROVED while the customer has no creator access —
the most confusing support ticket this feature could produce.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE
────────────────────────────────
The updated application, same shape as `3. Review queue`.
status is now APPROVED and reviewedBy carries the admin email.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
404 — no such application
409 — already approved or rejected. Two admins (or two browser tabs)
      acting on the same row: the second one is told plainly rather
      than silently overwriting the first.
409 — that customer is already a creator

Gate 1, the other way.

────────────────────────────────
BODY
────────────────────────────────
reason   REQUIRED, 10-500 characters.
         ⚠️ This text is shown to the applicant VERBATIM, which is why
         a minimum length is enforced — "no" cannot be submitted.
         Someone put effort into applying and deserves to know what to
         fix.

────────────────────────────────
WHAT HAPPENS
────────────────────────────────
The application becomes REJECTED, and the applicant cannot apply again
for 30 days. Their app shows the reason and the canReapplyAt date.

Without that cooling-off period the same person reapplies every morning
and the queue fills with names an admin has already judged.

────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE
────────────────────────────────
The updated application, with status REJECTED, rejectionReason set to
your text, and canReapplyAt 30 days out.

────────────────────────────────
ERRORS
────────────────────────────────
400 — reason shorter than 10 characters
404 — no such application
409 — already approved or rejected

item.name: Admin — Audit log
item.description:
There is one admin, so "who did it?" is a small question.
"WHEN, and WHAT changed?" is the big one.

A customer asks "why was I blocked?" or "where did my wishlist go?" — this is
the only place that answers.

The actor and IP are filled in automatically by AdminContextInterceptor
(AsyncLocalStorage), so no service has to thread them through its arguments.
The alternative was an `actor` parameter on every method, and then whoever
writes the next method forgets it and the audit entry quietly disappears.

⚠️ AuditLog has NO foreign keys, on purpose: the history of a deleted or
merged record has to survive the record itself.
